newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU recommendations to Italy on budget deficit.
newsitem.headline: EU recommendations to Italy on budget deficit.

text.p: The following is the text of European Union finance ministers' recommendations to Italy concerning the country's excessive deficit:

"The Italian government should put an end to the present excessive deficit situation as rapidly as possible with a view to being prepared for participation in the third stage of EMU in accordance with the timetable and the procedures set out in the Treaty.

The Italian government sets the budgetary objectives for the following three years in the annual "Documento di programmazione economica-finanziaria" (DPEF); this document will be presented by the end of May to Parliament. The convergence programme, which will be based on the DPEF, will be presented to the Council immediately after. The Council welcomes the decision of the Italian Government to present this programme.

The Council notes that the government deficit in 1996 was 6.7% of GDP, only 0.3% percentage points below the previous year. It considers insufficient the control of general Government expenditure which, net of interest payments, increased well above the nominal rate of growth of the economy. As a consequence, the primary surplus narrowed from 4.4% in 1995 to 4.0% of GDP.

The Council notes that government debt ratio has declined slightly in the last two years to 123.7% of GDP in 1996, which is considerably above the Treaty reference value. These developments took place in a framework of much lower growth than expected in the budget.

The Council welcomes the Italian Government intention to reduce the deficit ratio to 3% of GDP in 1997, therefore accelerating the pace of adjustment previously targeted as recommended by the Council. The Council believes that this decision has contributed to increasing the confidence in the convergence process of the Italian economy. A departure from the consolidation target may seriously undermine this process, adding considerably to the adjustment effort required in the future.

For this reason the Council strongly encourages the Italian government to pursue its budgetary objectives for 1997 with determination and to monitor carefully the execution of the budget; it welcomes that additional measures have been introduced at the end of March 1997. Furthermore, the Council recommends the Italian government to achieve in 1998 a further reduction of the government deficit to well below 3% of GDP. Such a step is necessary to secure a durable budgetary adjustment, to progressively lessen the vulnerability of public finance to cyclical fluctuations and to hasten the reduction in the debt ratio.

The measures taken in 1997 which have a temporary nature should be replaced by structural measures with a permanent impact on the budget. The Council welcomes that, as a step towards this objective, the Italian Parliament is now on the basis of a Government proposal, completing legislation on structural reforms in the areas of taxation, central and local administration, civil service and State accounting procedures. The Council invites the Italian government to adopt the necessary measures to implement structural reforms as soon as possible.
This recommendation is addressed to the Italian Republic.
